# shorter and plainer (A2 English, short lists), each with its figures, its
# "Do it" task and ONE "Try it" set of varied questions (at least two thirds
# ask to apply: calculate, choose for a situation, decide). No repeated
# questions between sections.
#   60 min: 4–6 Try it, 15–28 questions.  90 min: 6–9 Try it, 30–45 questions.
# THE PAGE TEACHES (AUTHORING.md): every question has its answer at once.
# Every Try it question has a "Why:" reason; every Do it box has a
# ::: {.check} (the result and why; for a personal task, a model answer and a
# 2–3 point self-check). Task with AI: 0–2 boxes, only where AI lets students do more.
title: "Lesson title, as in the notes"
description: "One short line for the hero."
lesson: 1
ilos: [A1]
format: lesson-html

This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a problem in a game. Then it explains the idea behind it. It ends
with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. Every question on this page
has its answer: try first, then check.

The Do it task of the notes, in two or three short sentences.

::: {.check}
